perspective:
Arthur has access to the following information:

- He is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate. He knows Teresa Ortega is a medical assistant and professional colleague; they have collaborated before on community service projects.
- During this project, he observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He felt concerned and decided to offer help.
- He heard Teresa say she thought she could manage but had a lot to do. He told her to take care of herself and offered to help so they could finish faster. She accepted help organizing medical supplies; he agreed and began.
- He believed Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathy and wanted to reassure her. He told her he admired her self-reliance but that accepting help did not mean she was incapable. He heard her say she wanted to show she could do it herself. He emphasized teamwork and support; she said he was right and that she needed reminding.
- He later believed Teresa was still struggling and felt frustrated that his help was not yielding results. He wanted to support her without making her feel inadequate. He said he could see things were still tough and that she was doing a great job. She said she felt busy and behind. He proposed working together rather than just helping her; she agreed. He suggested tackling it as a team.
- He believed working together would ease her burden and improve efficiency. He felt hopeful and committed to the collaborative approach. He told Teresa he was hopeful it would make things easier; she said it already felt less overwhelming. He proposed handling inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. She agreed and said she was glad. He said he was too and wanted a productive day.
- He believed their teamwork paid off and strengthened their professional relationship. He felt satisfied and wanted to continue collaborating. He told Teresa they had accomplished more together; she agreed it was a great experience. He proposed continuing this approach in future projects. She called it a fantastic idea and said they had proven they were more efficient and effective as a team. He said they should keep it up and that he looked forward to their next project. She thanked him for being a supportive colleague.
